summary: This experimental RFC specifies signaling of additional Segment Routing Segment Types for SR Policies in BGP using the SR Policy SAFI.

eli5.summary: This adds more kinds of stops to the trip plans that BGP can carry.

subtitle: Adds the remaining Segment Types (C to K) to BGP's SR Policy SAFI for both SR-MPLS and SRv6.

tldr.problem: RFC 9830 let BGP carry SR Policies using only Segment Types A and B, but the SR Policy architecture (RFC 9256) defines more Segment Types.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a sub-TLV for each of Segment Types C through K, each with its own type code and length rules, and adds an A-Flag and S-Flag to the SR Policy Segment Flags.
tldr.outcome: BGP can now advertise all the Segment Types of RFC 9256 for SR-MPLS and SRv6. It is an Experimental RFC.

today: RFC 9831 was published in September 2025 as an Experimental RFC. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to the metadata, and it builds on RFC 9830.

sections.title: Why More Segment Types
sections.content:
The BGP Segment Routing (SR) Policy Subsequent Address Family Identifier (SAFI) was introduced by RFC 9830 to advertise SR Policies (RFC 8402). It covered only Segment Types A and B from the SR Policy Architecture (RFC 9256).

This document specifies how to advertise the remaining Segment Types in the SR Policy SAFI, for both SR-MPLS (RFC 8660) and Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6, RFC 8754 and RFC 8986). It does not change SR Policy operations or fault management from RFC 9830.
sections.eli5: BGP's trip-plan format only had two kinds of stop. This fills in the rest so every kind of stop from the rule book can be written down.

sections.title: Segment Lists and the Eleven Types
sections.content:
A Segment List sub-TLV encodes one explicit path toward the endpoint. A Segment sub-TLV describes a single element of that path. RFC 9256 defines these types:

  • A: SR-MPLS label. B: SRv6 SID.
  • C, D: IPv4 or IPv6 prefix with optional SR Algorithm (D is for SR-MPLS).
  • E: IPv4 prefix with local interface ID.
  • F, G, H: link endpoints as local and remote pairs, for SR-MPLS (IPv4 addresses, IPv6 prefix with interface IDs, IPv6 addresses).
  • I, J, K: the SRv6 counterparts of D, G and H.

Validating an explicit path is beyond the scope of BGP and is done by the Segment Routing Policy Module (SRPM). A mix of SR-MPLS and SRv6 segments makes the segment list invalid.
sections.eli5: Each kind of stop names a place differently: by a city address, by a road, or by both ends of a road. Some are for one kind of road system and some for another.

sections.title: The Segment Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
Each type has a sub-TLV with a Type, a Length counting the value only, a Flags octet and type-specific fields. Types C to H carry an optional 4-octet SR-MPLS SID (label, TC, S and TTL, as for Type A). Types I, J and K carry an optional 16-octet SRv6 SID and an optional 8-octet SRv6 Endpoint Behavior and SID Structure, which MUST NOT be included when the SID is absent.

Where a field is reserved it MUST be zero on transmission and ignored on receipt. The Length rules are strict: for example Type C MUST be 10 with the SID and 6 without, and Type K MUST be 58, 50 or 34 depending on which optional parts are present. In Type G the Remote Interface ID and remote node address MAY be zero when local data is enough to describe the link. In Types I to K the SRv6 SID may be 0 to indicate a desired behavior or structure without naming the SID.

TLV 12, used for Type K in early drafts of RFC 9830, has been deprecated to avoid backward-compatibility issues.
sections.eli5: Each stop has a label with its address pieces. Some pieces are optional, and the label says exactly how long it must be so nobody misreads it.

sections.title: SR Policy Segment Flags
sections.content:
The Flags octet holds the existing V-Flag and B-Flag from RFC 9830 plus two new flags. The A-Flag says the SR Algorithm field is meaningful. The S-Flag says an SR-MPLS or SRv6 SID is present.

  • The V-Flag applies to all Segment Types.
  • The A-Flag applies to Types C, D, I, J and K, and MUST be ignored for A, B, E, F, G and H.
  • The S-Flag applies to Types C through K, and MUST be ignored for A and B.
  • The B-Flag applies to Types B, I, J and K, and MUST be ignored for A, C, D, E, F, G and H.

When the A-Flag is not set, the SR Algorithm field MUST be zero on transmission and ignored on receipt.
sections.eli5: Little switches on each stop say whether an extra number or an extra address is included, and which stop kinds should pay attention to each switch.

sections.title: IANA, Security and Manageability
sections.content: IANA allocated code points in the SR Policy Segment List Sub-TLVs registry and the SR Policy Segment Flags registry, both under the BGP Tunnel Encapsulation registry group. The security considerations and the operations and manageability considerations of RFC 9830 apply to these Segment Types, and none are added.
sections.eli5: The official number list was updated, and the safety and management rules stay the same as before.

viz.caption: SEGMENT SUB-TLV CODE POINTS ALLOCATED BY RFC 9831

items.label: Type C
items.desc: IPv4 node address, optional SR Algorithm.

items.label: Type D
items.desc: IPv6 node address, optional SR Algorithm (SR-MPLS).

items.label: Type E
items.desc: IPv4 node address with local interface ID.

items.label: Type F
items.desc: Local and remote IPv4 link addresses.

items.label: Type G
items.desc: IPv6 local and remote nodes with interface IDs.

items.label: Type H
items.desc: Local and remote IPv6 link addresses.

items.label: Type J
items.desc: IPv6 nodes with interface IDs for SRv6.

items.label: Type K
items.desc: Local and remote IPv6 link addresses for SRv6.

items.title: A-Flag
items.text: The SR Algorithm field is present. Applies to Types C, D, I, J and K.

items.title: S-Flag
items.text: A SID is present. Applies to Types C through K.
